title: TAROT: Task-Adaptive Refinement of LLM-prior Graphs for Few-shot Tabular Learning

problem.claim: Few-shot tabular learning addresses applications where annotation is costly and sufficient samples for new tasks are difficult to collect.

gap.claim: Existing approaches incur computational overhead, raise privacy and compliance concerns, and largely overlook semantic relationships between features needed to construct a semantic graph.

contributions.claim: TAROT is a GNN-based framework that constructs and refines a task-adaptive semantic graph from structural and semantic prior for few-shot tabular learning.
TAROT uses a Unified Semantic Tabular Node Encoder to encode heterogeneous tabular data into unified node semantic representations.
TAROT uses LLM-inferred feature relationships and task-adaptive graph refinement to remove spurious or task-unrelated edges and add missing task-related edges before GNN message passing.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on various few-shot tabular learning benchmarks reportedly demonstrate superior performance.
The authors report TAROT as a state-of-the-art approach in few-shot tabular learning.

narrative_sequence.summary: Few-shot tabular learning is motivated by costly annotation and limited samples for new tasks.
Traditional and LLM-based methods have shown effectiveness, but each has computational, privacy, or compliance limitations.
Both paradigms largely overlook semantic relationships between features, despite their structural value for semantic graphs.
TAROT encodes tabular data, constructs an LLM-informed semantic graph, refines it for the task, and applies GNN message passing.
The authors report superior benchmark performance and state-of-the-art results.

source_observation.claim: Semantic relationships between features can provide structural and semantic prior for graph construction, while task-adaptive refinement can remove spurious edges and add task-related ones.

interpretation.claim: When an externally generated relational structure may contain task-irrelevant or hallucinated links, aligning and refining it against the downstream objective may improve its utility.

application.claim: This pattern may apply to few-shot settings that combine semantic priors, generated relations, and graph-based prediction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported few-shot tabular learning benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, baseline methods, or performance values.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported results.
The abstract does not quantify computational overhead, privacy protection, compliance benefits, or the effect of each TAROT component.
